newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: HORSE RACING-SWAIN TO RACE IN MELBOURNE CUP.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-SWAIN TO RACE IN MELBOURNE CUP.

text.p: Leading British stayer Swain heads a distinguished list of thoroughbreds nominated for this year's $A2.0 million ($US1.48) Melbourne Cup classic, race organisers said on Thursday.

Swain, who beat Helissio, Singspiel and Pilsudski to win last week's King George VI and Queen Elizabeth Diamond Stakes at Ascot, was among 22 northern hemisphere-trained horses to enter, the Victoria Racing Club said.
"The nomination of Swain is a coup for the racing industry in Victoria," the club said in a statement.
The Melbourne Cup handicap, to be run over 3,200 metres at Flemington on November 4, has attracted a growing number of overseas horses in recent years.
International interest in the race grew after Irish stayer Vintage Crop won in 1993, the first horse from outside Australasia to achieve the feat since it was first run in 1861.
Three of last year's Melbourne Cup runners from Europe -- beaten favourite Oscar Schindler, Double Trigger and Grey Shot, have been entered again, the club said.
